exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $95.2100 to $96.1900; spot sits at 36% of that range.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL is presently trading modestly higher at $95.56, up 0.32% in the last hour and 0.18% over twenty‑four hours, indicating short‑term buying pressure that is confirmed by the Chainlink feed at $95.65, a 0.09% premium to the spot quote, establishing a reliable entry level for a long practice position [Ex. A, G].  

2. Despite a seven‑day decline of 5.69%, the asset remains well within its 24‑hour range, sitting at only 36% of that band, and the realized volatility is a low 2.92% per day, suggesting a stable environment where a modest upside can be captured without excessive risk [Ex. B, C, D].  

3. Market sentiment is turning from fear toward neutrality, as the Fear & Greed Index has risen to 34 from 54 a week ago, indicating improving sentiment that typically precedes price appreciation, while liquidity remains robust at $1.3 billion, ensuring efficient execution [Ex. E, F].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is perched near the bottom of its 24‑hour range (36% of the $95.2100‑$96.1900 band) [Ex. B] while the seven‑day high sits 7.14% above current levels [Ex. C]; this price compression signals a likely rebound rather than a continuation of the modest 0.32% hourly gain [Ex. A].  

2. Realized volatility remains low at 2.92% per day [Ex. D] and liquidity is ample with $1.3 billion traded in the last 24 hours [Ex. E]; these conditions reduce downside risk and support a short‑term upward correction.  

3. Market sentiment has turned fearful, as the Fear & Greed Index fell to 34 from 54 a week ago [Ex. F], indicating oversold conditions that historically precede short‑term price recoveries.  

For these reasons the Bear respectfully requests that the Court deny the Bull’s motion and keep the practice position open. The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first claim rests on a superficial reading of the 24‑hour range; the spot sits at 36 % of that band yet is merely 0.32 % above the lower bound, offering no momentum catalyst—price has been sliding 5.69 % over seven days [Ex. C] and remains below the 72‑hour average [Ex. C]. The second point ignores the neutral RSI of 41.4, which signals neither bullish nor bearish pressure [Ex. D]; low volatility alone does not imply upside, it merely reflects a stagnant market that can break lower. Consequently, the Bear’s arguments lack actionable evidence of a rebound. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first point rests on a negligible 0.32% hourly uptick that is statistically noise within a 2.92% daily volatility band; a 0.09% premium on the Chainlink feed does not constitute a sustainable entry signal [Ex. D, G]. The second point ignores the seven‑day downtrend of –5.69% and the fact that today’s spot sits 7.14% below the week’s high, indicating lingering bearish pressure despite being mid‑range [Ex. C, B]. These contradictions outweigh any modest buying bias. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds short‑term downside bias for SOL/USD

findings.finding: Spot price up 0.32% hour and 0.18% day, indicating minimal short‑term buying pressure
Seven‑day decline of 5.69% and price 7.14% below weekly high shows persistent bearish trend
RSI at 41.4 is neutral and low volatility (2.92%) suggests lack of strong momentum
Fear & Greed Index at 34 (fear) down from 54 indicates worsening sentiment

ruling.opinion: The week‑long downtrend and heightened fear outweigh the modest hourly gain and neutral momentum, signaling likely further pullback. Low volatility and mid‑range positioning do not provide a bullish catalyst, so a short practice position is justified. [Ex. C, F, D, A]
ruling.dissent: The Bull argues that the narrow range and low volatility create a stable environment for modest upside, but the prevailing bearish trend and fear sentiment dominate the short‑term outlook.
